title: Wang2026: Sensory-guided joint-learning MI-BCI study from Wang et al. (2026)
description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recordings from 39 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing a longitudinal online motor imagery brain-computer interface study with 1D and 2D cursor control. Participants imagined left-hand, right-hand, bilateral-hand movements or rest across multiple sessions. Cohorts differed in feedback: sensory-guided joint learning with tactile stimulation and EEGNet adaptation, BCI2000 control, tactile control, and EEGNet control. The data support research on how sensory guidance and co-adaptive decoding speed the acquisition of BCI control.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 62 channels with a Compumedics Neuroscan SynAmps 2/RT amplifier and Quik-Cap, using BCI2000 for stimulus presentation and online control. Each regular session had six runs, plus a separate initial BCI2000 baseline run. Participants completed 4, 6, or 8 sessions. Online decoding used a weighted EEGNet, EEGNet, or a fixed BCI2000 linear classifier depending on cohort. Data are trial-segmented with a 60 Hz notch filter.
